devices.description: List of EnerGenie devices to configure. Each entry defines a single device with its name, protocol, IP, port, and password. Required fields correspond exactly to the documented fields in the egctl(1) configuration file format: name, protocol, IP, port, password. Order matters: devices appear in /etc/egtab in this order, and egctl uses the first matching name when invoked with that name. No nested objects — flat structure per device entry as documented (space/tab-delimited line). Items contain only scalar values or bare arrays where needed (none here). See example: device list with two devices in sample_values. See documentation: egctl(1) CONFIGURATION section, 5 fields per device, comment lines ignored, blank lines ignored, tab/space separators allowed. Use 'pms20' for EG-PMS-LAN, 'pms21' for EG-PMS2-LAN. Port is TCP port of the Power Manager client (default 5000 per examples). Password is plain text per documentation (egctl does not support masked passwords). No validation beyond documented allowed protocols and required fields — egctl handles validation at runtime (not required here). All fields are required per documentation and sample config. Omitting any field breaks egctl config parsing. Use only documented protocols: pms20, pms21. Use bare string for ip (IPv4 only per examples; IPv6 not documented). Use integer for port as documented. Password may be empty but default is provided as empty string to match examples that show passwords explicitly (e.g., hackme). Per docs, password is the 5th field and required in config even if blank. Example config includes passwords; blank passwords not shown but allowed per field count requirement. Use empty string as default to allow omitting or leaving blank in template rendering while keeping config valid. Use literal string for name to avoid unintended interpolation. All fields are mandatory per egctl(1) config syntax. No extra fields beyond documented 5 per line. Comment added above each entry for clarity.
